name: Calibration of capsule SPRTs and rhodium-iron thermometers at the ITS-90 triple points of e-H2, Ne, O2 and Ar (13.8033-83.8058 K) in sealed cells in a vacuum-isolated closed-cycle cryostat
plain_name: Calibrate small cryogenic thermometers at the melting points of frozen hydrogen, neon, oxygen and argon
description: This is the BIPM CCT guide procedure. Sealed cells sit inside isothermal shields within a vacuum jacket, cooled by a cryocooler, and are melted with intermittent heat pulses.
keywords: Calibrate small cryogenic thermometers at the melting points of frozen hydrogen, neon, oxygen and argon

sources.citation: BIPM CCT Guide to the Realization of the ITS-90: Cryogenic Fixed Points (2018)

reported_equipment: two-stage closed-cycle cryocooler triple-point cryostat (Figure 7, PTB)
INRIM sealed cells models A, B and C

requirements.rationale: The four triple points span 13.8033 K to 83.8058 K.
The hydrogen has to be frozen below 13.8033 K.
The cell must be in a vacuum jacket.
Heat pulses and thermometer readout need electrical leads.
Closed-cycle cryocoolers are preferred but not required.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
